thread:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] geo-dns: elevated resolver failures affecting eu-west-2 (detected 2026-03-15T11:02:30Z). Observed spike in SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN for *.redwood-inference.net. Pager routed to #oncall-sre.
alex: acked. I'm pulling resolver metrics + ikey logs. Any recent Route53/CF changes?
mika: i didn't touch DNS; I rolled a canary of route53 health-check patch 30m ago, but only enabled for internal checks. tagging @sre_lead
sre_lead: seeing 4.9% NXDOMAIN on resolver-probes-eu for the last 8m. latency up too. Suspect external resolver/backplane. Cloudflare resolver latency spikes in eu-west
cloudops: checking cloud provider network events... aws eu-west-2 reported one az net blip ~11:00 but nothing on DNS. Cloudflare status shows partial resolver degradation in EU ~11:01
alex: running dig against our NS from a couple public resolvers
alex: ```
# dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.net
SERVFAIL
# dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.net
203.0.113.42
# dig +short @213.199.219.0 api.redwood-inference.net
;; connection timed out;
```
mika: interesting — mixed responses. could be resolver caching + propagation + intermittent upstream timeouts
blake: jumps in route53 healthcheck failures for eu-edge (~11:00) correlate with resolver failures. maybe healthcheck origin path uses a regional IP that's flapping
kevin-cs: customers reporting 502s in EU region - ticket surge from eu customers, about 30 incidents in last 20m
alex: quick impact calc: ~3% of production reads in EU failing DNS -> 2% of API calls returning 502s. I'll mark customer impact as partial regional outage and notify status page
sre_lead: mitigation options: 1) adjust GeoDNS to prefer us-east fallback for eu-west queries (lower affinity) 2) increase TTLs and force fallback CNAME to global-host 3) temp reweight Route53 records to healthy endpoints
alex: doing a controlled reweight to shift 30% of traffic to us-east (Route53 weights) now
alex: ```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.net","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east","Weight":70,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"203.0.113.42"}],"TTL":60}}]}'
```
deploy-bot: Change submitted (chg-4578). Propagation in progress.
mika: also disabling the new health-check canary to remove circuit-triggered failovers
mika: ```
# aws route53 disable-health-check --health-check-id h-abc123
```
cloudops: Adding a short term resolver-level workaround: spinning up local forwarding resolvers in eu-west that forward to 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 with retries
blake: sanity check logs: upstream resolver error patterns show SERVFAIL with DO bit set for EDNS0 > payload size; maybe a broken middlebox dropping large UDP responses -> fallback to TCP needed
alex: enabling TCP fallback on our resolver forwarders + increase EDNS buffer size
sre_lead: status page note: "Partial DNS failures affecting some EU customers; mitigations in progress. Next update in 10m". Kevin, can you message affected customers with workaround (retry or region pin to us-east)?
kevin-cs: on it. sending template and tagging affected customers in CS dashboard
mika: monitoring metrics — NXDOMAIN down to 2.1% after partial reweight. Latency improving slowly
alex: last check from external probes: 1.2% failed. Looks like reweight + resolver forwarders helping. Keeping incident open for 45m to verify stability
sre_lead: handoff to night oncall in 30m. @mika you'll do the handoff notes please
mika: creating handoff summary:
- root cause: external DNS/resolver failures and possible EDNS/middlebox truncation causing SERVFAIL in EU
- mitigation: Route53 weight rebalancing (70/30 us-east), disabled canary health-check, local forwarding resolvers with TCP fallback, status page update
- customer impact: partial EU customers saw DNS resolution failures -> ~2% API error rate -> several tickets filed
- next steps: monitor for 2 hours, revert weights gradually after stable 30m window, follow up with Cloudflare/AWS on resolver logs
mika: handing off to night oncall @blake in 30m. will ping again on stable state
blake: ack, will take over. leaving notes in incident tracker INC-211234
IncidentBot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, owner=alex, severity=partial-regional-impact
kevin-cs: update to customers sent. no major customers escalated to SEs yet. monitoring replies
alex: closing out active mitigation; will keep watch. final timestamp 11:22 UTC for now. add postmortem if recurrence
sre_lead: adding postmortem task. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
